before.rappels: Four single-rope rappels down the ascent route
before.beta: From the col between Mount Stuart and Sherpa Peak, ascend the ridge generally trending climber's left. With a 60m rope you can reach the first belay in a cave-like feature with a platform large enough for several climbers; the crux is the crack leading out of the cave (rated 5.4-5.5). A second pitch leads to another anchor, after which a short 4th-class scramble gains the notoriously airy summit block. Descent is 4 single-rope rappels down the ascent line.
before.descent: Reverse the route with a short rappel off the summit block, then descend the approach slopes.

itinerary.cal: Best late June through September once the Longs Pass approach and rock are snow-free; the Teanaway River Road trailhead is usually accessible by early June.

days.note: From the Longs Pass Trailhead, climb over Longs Pass (6,200 ft), drop to the Ingalls Creek basin, then climb back up talus and slab to a flat bivy spot near 'Table Rock' at treeline below Sherpa's west side. Most parties take 6-7 hours with overnight and rock gear.
days.title: Approach to treeline bivy
days.objective: Reach camp near 'Table Rock' (~7,400 ft) below the West Ridge

days.note: Leave camp before dawn, scramble to the base of the ridge, then climb 5-6 pitches (5.4 with a crux that feels more like 5.5) to the summit block. Reverse the ridge with a short rappel, then descend all the way back over Longs Pass to the trailhead — a long 12-14 hour day.

waypoints.name: Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Way Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd, FR-9737) via Longs Pass
waypoints.note: Shared trailhead for Longs Pass Trail and Esmeralda Basin/Ingalls Way Trail; route drops from Longs Pass into Ingalls Creek drainage before climbing to Sherpa's east basin.
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Fork Teanaway Road (FR-9737) to its end at the Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Way trailhead. This is the shared lot for the Longs Pass Trail and the Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Way Trail, and it is the same trailhead the West Ridge uses; for the East Ridge you want the Longs Pass Trail (FST 1391), which goes over Longs Pass at about 6,200 ft and down to Ingalls Creek. Plan on late June through September, once that Longs Pass and Ingalls Creek approach is snow-free.

before.overview: New York Gully splits the NW Face of Snoqualmie Mountain, the most-climbed of five parallel ice/mixed lines on that wall (alongside Pineapple Express, Blue Moon, New York Gully Direct, and LA Express). First climbed by Jim Ruche and Bob Cotter in February 1991 as a IV 5.8 A2 WI4 aid line, it's a roughly 1,300-ft alpine route following a prominent gully system to a distinctive 'box gully' feature, finishing with a steep corner pitch that was originally aided and first freed in 2004 at M5+/6-.
